## Highlights since 0.15.2

- **Code files in your project.** Python and common code and configuration files (JavaScript, Rust, Go, C and C++, Java, Ruby, R, shell scripts, JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, CSS, SQL and more) can be created, dropped in, searched and attached to the agent, and their editors offer autocompletion.
- **Switch Overleaf accounts.** After signing out you can sign in with a different account. Sign out and Cancel now really end a sign-in in progress, and ⌘Z and ⇧⌘Z work in the sign-in window.
- **The agent panel remembers your setup.** Your default provider, model, effort, hidden providers, provider order and drafts are kept across launches, and Settings → Agent providers has a Default provider row.

## Notable fixes

- Hovering a command inside a formula no longer opens its description over the live math preview.
- Versions shows the right timeline and restores correctly for a project inside a larger Git repository, and a refused restore no longer leaves a stray auto-saved version.
- Zoomed panels stay on screen in narrow windows.
- The terminal no longer freezes on heavy output when it opens.
- A pipe or other special file ending in .pdf no longer stalls PDF reading.
- Literature search no longer answers from an out-of-date index after two searches clash.
- The app starts with a little less code to load.
